Firstly, the mechanism of twin strengthening and toughening. Previous studies [10,57] have shown that the strengthening of TiAl alloys is owing to twinning during cold deformation, which provides new interfaces that can impede dislocation motion. Twinning is similar to refining grain size, which helps to increase plasticity

Thirdly, grain refinement. It is commonly recognized that the correlation between grain size and yield strength follows the Hall-Petch model ... In this study, the introduction of LaB6 markedly reduced the lamellar colony size (Fig. 5), which resulted in an increase in the number of interfaces hindering dislocation movement and coordinated deformation as shown in Fig. 10 (f). Therefore, the strength and plasticity of TiAl/LaB6 composites are increased owing to the fine grain effect

Secondly, precipitate phase reinforcement. Fig. 10 (d) shows (Ti, Nb) B and La2O3 phases near the tensile fracture of the as-sintered TiAl-0.10LaB6 composite, where there is a high density of dislocation entanglement around the two phases
